[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Maximum Crossings (Hard Version)** [CF 1676H2 · Maximum Crossings (Hard Version)](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1676/H2){rating="1500"}

Two wires $i < j$ cross exactly when their bottom ends are in the opposite order: always if $a_i > a_j$, never if $a_i < a_j$, and, if $a_i = a_j$, whenever we put $i$'s end to the right of $j$'s on the shared segment, which we can do for all such pairs at once. So the answer is the number of pairs $i < j$ with $a_i \ge a_j$: an **inversion count** in which ties count. Merge sort counts it in $O(n\log n)$; the only change from the textbook count is that the merge must take the *right* head on ties.

[Solved in full in @sec-salgo-p2-a.]{.card-link}
